intro: Martial arts and combat sports in Illinois happen in real rooms. Some are storefronts in strip malls with a dojo or dojang sign. Some are high school wrestling rooms down a hallway. Others are boxing gyms, college judo clubs and park district field houses. Each room has its own name, its own rule book and its own way of paying the rent.

In this unit you will visit those rooms through their history. You will trace words like dojo, dojang and kwoon back to Japan, Korea and Guangdong. You will meet the Chicago Tribune's Golden Gloves, the 1905 South Park field houses, Hull-House and the IHSA state wrestling series. You will see when doors opened to girls and women, and which laws helped.

By the end, you will be able to compare two training rooms. You will name who writes each room's rules, who pays for it and who could walk in, with dates. You will also read a trophy, bracket or program as a historian reads an artifact.
bigQuestion: Who built the rooms where Illinois young people box, wrestle and train, and who decided the rules inside them?

timeline.t: The Queensberry Rules for boxing are published in London
Kanō Jigorō founds the Kodokan judo school in Tokyo
Jane Addams and Ellen Gates Starr open Hull-House in Chicago
The Illinois High School Association is founded
Chicago's South Park Commission opens neighborhood parks with field houses
Five Midwest states found the group that becomes the NFHS, meeting in Chicago
Tunney and Dempsey fight before more than 100,000 people at Soldier Field
Chicago's 22 park districts join into the Chicago Park District
The IHSA crowns its first boys state wrestling champions
Robert Trias opens a karate school in Phoenix, Arizona
Congress passes Title IX; the Kukkiwon opens in Seoul
The IHSA holds its first girls state wrestling finals

test.q: Which word for a training hall comes from Cantonese?
test.why: Kwoon is the Cantonese form of guan, a word for hall.

test.q: What did the word dojo name before it named sports halls?
test.why: Dojo first named the place of the Buddha's awakening and later temple halls.

test.q: When did the IHSA crown its first boys state wrestling champions?
test.why: The IHSA's first boys state wrestling champions were crowned in 1937.

test.q: In which city was the NFHS founded in 1920?
test.why: Leaders from five Midwest states met in Chicago in 1920.

test.q: Where did karate grow before it reached mainland Japan?
choices: Okinawa, in the old Ryukyu Kingdom
test.why: Karate grew on Okinawa, once the center of the Ryukyu Kingdom.

test.q: Who coached the first U.S. Olympic judo team in 1964?
test.why: Yosh Uchida of San Jose State coached the 1964 U.S. judo team.

test.q: Which law required each U.S. Olympic sport to have its own national governing body?
choices: the Immigration and Nationality Act of 1965
test.why: The Amateur Sports Act of 1978 created separate national governing bodies.

test.q: Which newspaper editor backed the Chicago Golden Gloves and created baseball's first All-Star Game?
test.why: Arch Ward of the Chicago Tribune backed the Golden Gloves and created the 1933 All-Star Game.

test.q: What did the 1905 South Park field houses give crowded neighborhoods?
choices: public indoor rooms with gyms, showers and libraries
test.why: The field houses held gyms, locker rooms, showers, club rooms and library branches.

test.q: Which bout at Soldier Field in 1927 drew more than 100,000 people?
test.why: Gene Tunney beat Jack Dempsey there on September 22, 1927.

test.q: How does a school wrestling room differ from a storefront dojo in who pays?
choices: Public school funds pay for the wrestling room; tuition pays for the storefront
The IHSA pays the storefront's rent
test.why: School rooms are paid mostly by public funds; storefronts depend on tuition and fees.

test.q: When did women's judo become an Olympic medal sport?
test.why: Women's judo became an Olympic medal sport at Barcelona in 1992.

test.q: How many park districts were joined into the Chicago Park District in 1934?
test.why: Chicago joined its 22 separate park districts in 1934.

test.q: What was the first year of IHSA girls state wrestling finals?
test.why: The IHSA held the first girls state wrestling finals in 2022, at the end of the 2021–22 season.

test.q: Why do historians call a Golden Gloves program an artifact?
choices: It is an object made by people that survives from the past
test.why: An artifact is a human-made object from the past that historians can read.

write.prompt: Choose two rooms from this unit, such as an IHSA wrestling room and a Chicago Golden Gloves gym. Which room was more open to new people, and when? Cite at least two dated records from the unit, such as the 1937 and 2022 IHSA finals, Title IX (1972) or the 1905 field houses.
tips: Name each record you use and give its date.
Say who wrote the rules for each room and who paid for it.
Compare the two rooms fairly; describe changes over time with dates.
Use unit words such as governing body, amateur, bracket and field house.
